last_transition_reason: The argument correctly shows that for x,y in the same interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), both floor(nx) and floor(ny) equal m, and each floor(kx) is at most floor(ky) since x<=y and k>0. Hence F_n(x)-F_n(y) is a sum of nonnegative terms, proving F_n is nonincreasing on each such interval.
latest_nl_proof:
Fix n>1 and an integer m with 0<=m<=n-1. Let x,y be real numbers such that m/n<=x<=y<(m+1)/n. Then m<=nx<=ny<m+1, so floor(nx)=floor(ny)=m. Also, for each k=1,2,...,n, since x<=y and k>0 we have kx<=ky, hence floor(kx)<=floor(ky). Therefore
F_n(x)-F_n(y) = (floor(nx)-floor(ny)) - sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)-floor(ky))/k
= sum_{k=1}^n (floor(ky)-floor(kx))/k >= 0,
because each summand is nonnegative and each k is positive. Thus F_n(x)>=F_n(y), so F_n is nonincreasing on [m/n,(m+1)/n).
role_in_parent: Show that, on each interval [m/n,(m+1)/n), the maximum occurs at the left endpoint m/n.
statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k. For any integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1 and any real numbers x,y satisfying m/n <= x <= y < (m+1)/n, one has F_n(x) >= F_n(y).

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and satisfies n > 1
m is an integer satisfying 0 <= m <= n - 1
x and y are real numbers satisfying m/n <= x <= y and y < (m+1)/n
the upper endpoint (m+1)/n is excluded for y, and therefore also excluded for x because x <= y
k in the sum is an integer with 1 <= k <= n (so division by k is by a nonzero integer)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n > 1, the function Fn defined by Fn(t) = floor(n t) minus sum over integers k from 1 to n of floor(k t) divided by k is nonincreasing on each interval [m/n, (m+1)/n) in the sense that for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1 and for all real x and y with m/n <= x <= y < (m+1)/n, one has Fn(x) >= Fn(y).
quantifier_order: for all integers n greater than 1
for all integers m with 0 <= m <= n-1
for all real numbers x and y with m/n <= x <= y and y < (m+1)/n
